verdict: Credible bounded DEV performance improvement candidate, conditional on final-version and publication gates; not a proven phone fix.
findings: Both counterordered workers show weighted FPS improvement and fewer slow frames with all windows retained. Worker 2 has both candidate blocks faster than both original blocks.
Every measured window records 4 original versus 2 candidate fence/getSync pairs per rendered frame, identical full resolution and held-mining position with 66-69 impacts.

All eight actual end captures preserve scene, native hero, companion, HUD and lighting without an apparent regression. They are live phase-dependent screenshots, not a frozen whole-package pixel-exact comparison. Exact component preservation is established by separate occupancy, native and shared-HUD correctness reviews.

This is stronger bounded evidence than the earlier approximately 5% discard candidate that failed physical phone validation: larger repeated whole-package signal, reduced slow-frame totals in both workers, and independently identified redundant CPU/pass work. It still does not establish physical phone benefit.
limitations: Worker 1 drifts strongly from early to late blocks; balancing reduces linear order bias but cannot exclude nonlinear or host-load confounding. The 12 windows per worker are correlated within four fresh-context blocks, not 12 independent trials.
Candidate worker 1 retains a 546 ms spike versus original maximum 271 ms. No smoothness guarantee or resolved-stutter claim is warranted; p95 values remain variable.
The measured package combines occupancy revision, native empty-2D removal and shared HUD. These results do not isolate the marginal UI contribution.
Same instrumentation overhead per WebGL call is not equal total overhead when call counts differ. Counts are not GPU duration measurements.
Mac WebKit Apple GPU and emulated touch do not establish iPhone thermal, memory or driver behavior.

Final version, exact artifact identity, publisher review and applicable regression gates remain required before authorized DEV publication. Wider terrain strips remain a separate unproven experiment; default width 6 is retained.
